name: Whooping cough
rawContent:
# Whooping cough: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
Whooping cough (pertussis) is an acute, highly contagious respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis, classically presenting with paroxysmal cough and inspiratory whoop.

overview.definition: Whooping cough (pertussis) is an acute, highly contagious respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis, classically presenting with paroxysmal cough and inspiratory whoop.
overview.epidemiology: Most severe disease occurs in unvaccinated infants and pregnant/postpartum transmission chains.
overview.pathophysiology: Toxin-mediated airway inflammation causes prolonged cough and post-tussive vomiting.

atypicalPresentations: Afebrile prolonged cough in vaccinated adults

specialistTests: Public health notification and contact tracing pathway

diagnosis.criteria: Clinical suspicion with compatible prolonged/paroxysmal cough, supported by PCR positivity.

firstLine: Macrolide antibiotics (e.g. azithromycin) early in disease/course per local guidance
Supportive care: hydration, suctioning, oxygen if hypoxic
secondLine: Senior review for infants or severe disease
procedures: Escalate for ventilatory support if apnoeic/respiratory failure

monitoring: Safety-net for prolonged cough and transmission risk

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.notes: Most useful early and for reducing transmission.

content.prognosis: Most recover, but infants are at risk of severe complications.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Recognize prolonged paroxysmal cough patterns, start initial treatment, isolate appropriately, and involve paediatrics/public health early.
content.escalation: Escalate urgently for infant cases, apnoea, hypoxia, or poor oral intake.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Protect vulnerable contacts (especially infants and pregnant women), ensure notification as per local policy.
